Jewish section Campo Verano cemetery in Rome

Cemetery · Lazio, Italy

The Jewish section of Rome’s Campo Verano Cemetery was established in the 1890s and is an important site of memory for the city’s Jewish community. It contains elaborate family tombs, the historic Beit Tahara mortuary chapel, and memorials to Holocaust victims and Libyan Jews.

After the old Jewish cemetery on the Aventine Hill was destroyed in 1934, many historic tombs and monuments were transferred here. The cemetery’s ornate funerary art reflects the changing social and cultural life of Roman Jewry.

In front of the Beit Tahara stands a Holocaust memorial inaugurated in 1952, while a separate memorial dedicated to Jews who died in Libya was unveiled in 1977.
